topic: area and perimeter: correcting confusion between area and perimeter

traps.desc: multiplied the two side lengths, which counts the squares inside instead of the distance around
added all four sides, which measures the distance around instead of the squares inside
multiplied the length by the width, so the number found was the area and not the perimeter
added the four sides, so the number found was the perimeter and not the area
multiplied a side by itself, which fills the garden with squares instead of running fence around it
multiplied the two sides, which tells how much mat covers the floor rather than how much edging fits around it
compared the distances around instead of the space inside, and so reported no difference at all

problems.desc: Open task: draw two different rectangles on the grid that have the same perimeter but different areas, label both measurements on each, and write one sentence a classmate could use to decide whether a question is asking for area or perimeter. Read the drawings and the sentence by hand; many rectangle pairs are correct (for perimeter 16: 7 by 1 with area 7, 6 by 2 with area 12, 5 by 3 with area 15, 4 by 4 with area 16).
